bull.b: Six-month revenue growth indicates improving commercial performance despite a weaker quarter. Bellwright’s contribution and deferred-revenue conversion provide support for near-term sales, while the broader increase suggests the company can rebuild scale through content releases and platform expansion.

Meaningful engagement across PC, console and mobile gives Snail an established audience for future downloadable content, updates and monetization. A broad installed base can extend title lifecycles and reduce reliance on launching entirely new games for every revenue opportunity.

Positive TTM operating and free cash flow, together with higher unrestricted cash, improves the company’s ability to fund development and ongoing live operations. However, prior periods were inconsistent, so the benefit is meaningful but depends on whether cash generation can persist.

bear.b: Negative equity materially reduces financial flexibility and makes the balance sheet more dependent on continued access to financing or successful operating improvement. It also raises solvency and refinancing risk, limiting the company’s capacity to absorb setbacks or invest aggressively.

The company has not yet demonstrated durable profitability: revenue remains volatile and the TTM period still produced a net loss. Although margins improved from 2025, continued losses can constrain reinvestment, weaken resilience, and make future performance highly dependent on successful title and DLC execution.

Conditional listing status creates a material structural risk for the business and its financing flexibility. Failure to rebuild equity or satisfy continuing requirements could lead to delisting, potentially reducing market access and complicating capital-raising efforts needed to support operations.
